papers.title: Binary Belief Propagation Fixed Points: Finiteness, Rigidity, and Topological Complexity
papers.abstract: A fixed finite binary Ising model has only finitely many admissible complex belief propagation fixed points, even at degenerate parameter values. Families of positive fixed points obtained by varying external fields can nevertheless have nontrivial topology. We study this distinction through the external-field projection. For a fixed field, we prove finiteness by bounding the pole orders of the magnetizations on a hypothetical complex solution curve. The generic degree on the support graph then bounds the total local multiplicity. A graph has a single smooth real line as its full positive response for every choice of positive couplings, base field, and strictly positive sweep direction exactly when it contains no two vertex-disjoint connected subgraphs of cycle rank at least two. Two such subgraphs suffice to create a circular component. For a plane obtained by varying two vertex fields, connected simple bipartite cubic graphs with one uniform coupling and a universal bound on the fixed fields realize every genus. The minimum number of vertices grows logarithmically in the genus, by a matching algebraic upper bound on Betti numbers. Finally, we certify the complete field discriminant of an eighteen-vertex product model and recover its torus component's genus from the counts of distinct roots on all field cells. The three main theorems, including the logarithmic size bounds, are formally verified in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

papers.title: When is Polynomial Optimization SoS-Exact? Sufficient Regularization and Strict Gram Representations
papers.abstract: Global minimization of multivariate polynomials is computationally difficult in general, and nonnegativity does not necessarily imply a sum-of-squares (SoS) representation. We show that adding sufficiently strong Euclidean regularization to a polynomial provides a general mechanism for overcoming such challenges. Namely, for any multivariate polynomial $P$ of degree at most $p$ with a nonzero linear coefficient, and any even integer $2d>p$, we prove that $m_\sigma(s)=P(s)+\frac{\sigma}{2d}\|s\|_2^{2d}$ is SoS exact for all sufficiently large $\sigma$. Furthermore, the shifted polynomial $m_\sigma-\min m_\sigma$ admits a positive-definite Gram representation on appropriately-shifted nonconstant monomials. Consequently, the global minimum and minimizer can be recovered exactly by a single degree-$d$ semidefinite programming (SDP) representation, whose size is polynomial in the dimension for fixed $d$, without requiring higher levels of the SoS hierarchy. The proof develops a degree-independent mechanism based on the Bregman remainder of the regularizer: its strict Gram margin absorbs the lower-degree polynomial perturbations. We further establish an analogous exact SDP regime for polynomial optimization over sufficiently small Euclidean balls, connecting large regularization with small-radius trust-region problems. Finally, we investigate how the algebraic structure of the regularizer governs the existence of a strict Gram margin, extending the mechanism beyond Euclidean norms while identifying limitations of coordinate-separable regularization.

papers.title: On the gradient conjecture at infinity: Finite spherical length for gradient trajectories of definable potentials
papers.abstract: We prove that for every open $U \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ the spherical projection of every gradient trajectory $\theta(t)$, $t \geq 0$, of a definable $C^1$-potential $F \colon U \to \mathbb{R}$ has finite length and, in particular, converges (directional convergence). In other words, every gradient trajectory of a definable $C^1$-potential has finite total angular motion. Here, definable means definable in an arbitrary o-minimal structure expanding the real field. Notably, the gradient trajectory in this result is an arbitrary solution of the gradient flow differential equation (whose solutions may not be unique) with no further assumptions: The gradient trajectory may be unbounded and diverge to infinity or it may be convergent. The established theorem therefore provides affirmative answers to both the gradient conjecture at infinity for definable potentials and the definable Thom gradient conjecture. We extend our conclusions from the Euclidean metric to a general class of ambient metrics including Riemannian metrics and we establish uniform local upper bounds for the lengths of the spherical projections of gradient flow trajectories. We finally apply our findings to the training of deep neural networks (DNNs) to conclude that, in the case of definable and continuously differentiable activation and loss functions, the spherical projection of the DNN training flow must always converge (directional convergence).

papers.title: Finite Subgroups of Birational Automorphism Groups of Severi--Brauer Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that a finite group acting birationally on a non-trivial Severi--Brauer surface $S$ over a field $\mathbb{K}$ of positive characteristic not equal to $3$ is isomorphic either to a subgroup of group of biregular automorphisms of $S_{\mathbb{K}^{per}}$ or to a subgroup of $\mu^3_3$, where $\mu_3$ is a cyclic group of order $3$ and $\mathbb{K}^{per}$ is the perfect closure of a field $\mathbb{K}$. Combined with results about classification of finite subgroups of the group of biregular automorphisms of $S$, this gives a classification of finite subgroups of the group of birational automorphisms of $S$.

papers.title: On deformations of foliated complex analytic structures IV-1: Obstructed and unobstructed foliated deformations
papers.abstract: We study obstructions of deformations of foliated complex analytic structures. We describe obstructions in terms of Cech resolutions. From foliated complex analytic families in Part I and unfolded complex analytic families in Part III, we deduce the integrability conditions. We identify infinitesimal deformations and obstructions in terms of Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes from the integrability conditions. Then we describe the correspondences of infinitesimal deformations and obstructions between Cech resolutions, and Dolbeault resolutions or Dolbeault type bicomplexes.

papers.title: Adaptive visualization for enumerative problems
papers.abstract: We present an adaptive visualization framework and its implementation in the julia package AdaptiveVisualization.jl. Our algorithm visualizes functions using an adaptive sampling procedure that concentrates the evaluation budget at interesting regions of the domain. We illustrate our package on our main application: visualizing parameter spaces of enumerative problems.

papers.title: Automorphisms of Kummer and Artin-Schreier curves defined by Chebyshev polynomials
papers.abstract: Let phi_m be the monic Chebyshev polynomial characterized by phi_m(t + t^-1) = t^m + t^-m. We study the geometric automorphism groups of the smooth projective models of y^n = phi_m(x) and y^p - y = phi_m(x). We classify the hyperelliptic family in genus at least two, in characteristic zero and odd characteristic. For every m >= 5, with p not dividing m in positive characteristic, we determine the projective stabilizer of the roots of phi_m together with infinity. For tame Kummer covers, we describe the normalizer of the cyclic deck group and compute it explicitly for m >= 6. It is the full group when m > 2n. If m >= 3 and n > 2m, the full group has order 2n in characteristic zero and in every characteristic prime to 2nm. The proof uses the dihedral Galois closure of the map to the y-line and Dickson's subgroup classification. In odd characteristic, we also classify all Artin-Schreier curves in the family with genus at least two. For m >= 3 prime to p >= 5, the group has order 2p. In characteristic three, exactly five degrees are exceptional. We give the groups and their actions, and treat the quadratic cases separately.

papers.title: Metric nefness of direct image sheaves under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms
papers.abstract: We investigate the nefness of the direct image sheaves of relative adjoint bundles under weakly semi-stable K\"ahler morphisms between complex spaces. We show that the direct image sheaves are locally free and that their tautological line bundles are metrically nef, strengthening the previously known results on torsion-freeness and certain weak positivity.

papers.title: Birational Geometry of K-Moduli Spaces of Genus Four Curves
papers.abstract: We study the wall-crossings for K-moduli spaces of (3,3)-curves on $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$. Together with the boundary polarized Calabi--Yau moduli space, these spaces interpolate between the GIT moduli space of (3,3)-curves and the Baily--Borel compactification of the moduli space of K3 surfaces arising as cyclic triple covers of $\mathbb{P}^1\times\mathbb{P}^1$ branched along such curves. As applications, we describe the corresponding birational models in the Hassett--Keel--Looijenga program and realize the K-moduli space of degree one del Pezzo surfaces through explicit wall-crossings.

papers.title: Extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces without Gaussian maps and classification of prime Fano threefolds
authors: with an appendix written jointly with Anand Deopurkar
papers.abstract: In arXiv:2409.03960 an approach to the question of extendability of projective varieties via degeneration to ribbons was introduced, and in arXiv:2503.12661 it was used to give a new proof of optimal results on the extendability of general non-prime $K3$ surfaces and the classification of non-prime Fano threefolds. In this article we treat the prime case. We give a new proof of the optimal results on the extendability of general prime $K3$ surfaces of every genus, of the classification of prime Fano threefolds of Picard rank one due to Fano, Iskovskikh and Mukai, and of the irreducibility of their Hilbert schemes. This involves degenerations of $K3$ surfaces to ribbons on embedded rational normal scrolls, called $K3$ carpets. We compute exactly the cohomology of the twisted normal bundle of these $K3$ carpets, instead of computing coranks of Gaussian maps of the canonical curve sections. The key challenge is to analyze the coboundary map of the sequence relating the normal bundle of the $K3$ carpet to the normal bundle of the scroll. We give a deformation theoretic interpretation of this map. Given such a $K3$ carpet and its hyperplane section, which is a canonical ribbon, we show that the coboundary map corresponds to the obstruction to lifting a first order deformation of the underlying scroll fixing the underlying rational normal curve to a first order deformation of the $K3$ carpet fixing the canonical ribbon. To compute the obstruction, we use a result on extensions of non-split ribbons on any curve to a unique $K$-trivial carpet in a canonical way.

papers.title: The moduli stack of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type
papers.abstract: The goal of this article is the classification of affine bundles with fixed linearisation type over a compact complex manifold $X$. More precisely, let $E$ be a fixed holomorphic vector bundle over $X$ and $\mathcal{E}$ the associated locally free sheaf. We will assume that there exists an effective divisor $D$ on $X$ such that $H^1(X,\mathcal{E}(D))=0$. This condition is always satisfied when $X$ is a projective complex manifold. We define in a natural way the moduli stack of affine bundles on $X$ whose linearisation is isomorphic to $E$, and we prove that this moduli stack is isomorphic to the quotient stack $\big[H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)/H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D))\ltimes \mathrm{Aut}(E)\big]$ of the complex vector space $H^0(X,\mathcal{E}(D)_D)$ by the semi-direct product of the automorphism group $\mathrm{Aut}(E)$ (which is always an affine algebraic group) by the complex vector space $H^0(X,{\cal E}(D))$. Our isomorphism is obtained by constructing explicitly comparison functors $\mathscr{A}$, $\mathscr{T}$ between the two stacks and explicit natural isomorphisms $\mathscr{A}\circ\mathscr{T}\stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{id}$, $\mathrm{id} \stackrel{\simeq}{\longrightarrow}\mathscr{T}\circ\mathscr{A}$.

papers.title: Unramified case of Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms
papers.abstract: The Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture on quadratic forms asserts that any rationally isotropic nondegenerate quadratic form over a semilocal regular domain with $2$ invertible is isotropic. We prove the Colliot-Th\'el\`ene conjecture for semilocal regular domains that are geometrically regular over a discrete valuation ring with $2$ invertible. In particular, this includes unramified regular local rings of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, where $p\neq 2$.

papers.title: A Lefschetz Alternative for Real Characters on Smooth Quasi-Projective Varieties
papers.abstract: We establish a Lefschetz alternative for real characters on smooth complex quasi-projective varieties, extending Simpson's classical theorem beyond the compact K\"ahler setting. More precisely, for a nonzero real character of the fundamental group of a smooth connected complex quasi-projective variety, either the character factors through a holomorphic fibration onto a Riemann orbifold with connected general fiber, or every level set of an associated primitive function on the corresponding covering is connected and its inclusion induces a surjection onto the fundamental group of the covering. Our approach combines logarithmic holomorphic $1$-forms with a geometric flow construction to overcome the difficulties arising from noncompactness. Meanwhile, we prove a quasi-projective analogue of the Napier--Ramachandran theorem, showing that an epimorphism onto $\Z $ whose kernel is not finitely generated must factor through a hyperbolic Riemann orbifold. As applications, we derive several new restrictions on the structure of quasi-projective groups.

papers.title: Finite torsion in Hodge--Witt cohomology groups
papers.abstract: For a bounded coherent complex of graded modules over the Raynaud ring $R$, we compare three descriptions of finite torsion: Ekedahl's pieces $A_f^2$ and $A_{\SSpart}^1$ of the biduality filtration, the nilpotent and semisimple parts of the torsion of the Illusie--Raynaud c\oe ur, and the corresponding parts of the finite torsion $t^1$ of Ekedahl's diagonal cohomology. We show that finite torsion in bidegree $(0,i+1)$ measures the failure of the $i$th flat Artin--Mazur formal group to be smooth; we deduce that all flat Artin--Mazur formal groups of a Mazur--Ogus variety are smooth. For a smooth projective surface, we identify the three possible dual pairs in terms of the $p$-primary torsion of the geometric N\'eron--Severi group and the local-local and local-\'etale parts of the finite Picard quotient.

papers.title: All-genus mirror symmetry for the type-$D$ minimal resolution Calabi-Yau threefold
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the product of a minimal resolution of a binary dihedral surface singularity with an equivariant line, with volume-preserving scalar action. We identify its stable equivariant descendant Gromov--Witten theory and its free energies in genus at least two with the sign-sector topological recursion of the degenerate type-$D$ relativistic Toda spectral curve. The $R-$matrix calibration is determined at a partial large-radius limit, where the trivalent exceptional curve retains a nonzero K\"ahler parameter, while the remaining parameters vanish. The limiting theory on the mirror side is a sum of twisted point theories and the local $(-2,0)$ curve theory. Moreover, we identify the equivariant K-group supported on the surface zero section with an integral relative homology group of the mirror. Explicit cycles for the dual tautological bundles realize their Gamma central charges and all stable Gamma-framed descendants.

papers.title: Classification of 3-dimensional complex nilmanifolds - Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces
papers.abstract: We classify complex nilmanifolds of dimension three by describing the Teichm\"uller and moduli spaces of left-invariant complex structures for every real six-dimensional nilmanifold.

papers.title: Derived invariance of the space of holomorphic two-forms
papers.abstract: Let $\Phi:D^b(X)\to D^b(Y)$ be a derived equivalence between smooth projective complex varieties, and let $h=c_1(L)$ for an ample line bundle $L$ on $X$. For $z\in\mathbb{C}$, transporting the cup-product action and evaluating at $e^{zh}$ gives a homomorphism of graded algebras $\Theta^\bullet_{F,z}:H^\bullet(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\to H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$, where $F$ is the cohomological transform of $\Phi$. We prove that $\Theta^\bullet_{F,i}$ is an isomorphism in degrees one and two. In particular, $X$ and $Y$ have the same number of holomorphic two-forms. The proof in degree two uses the Hodge-Riemann bilinear relations on $X$ and on $X\times X$. We also prove derived invariance of all Hodge numbers when $K_X$ is trivial and the conjugate of a holomorphic volume form belongs to the subalgebra of $H^\bullet(X,\mathcal O_X)$ generated in degrees one and two. In even dimension, the evaluation isomorphism allows us to compare the ranks of cup product by powers of symplectic two-forms on the Hochschild diagonals. These ranks determine the Hodge numbers individually.

papers.title: Zero-cycles on quotients of multiple double covers and their products
papers.abstract: We prove the 0-cycle form of the generalized Bloch conjecture for smooth projective models of subgroup quotients of multiple double covers of projective space, with smooth branch hypersurfaces and reduced simple normal crossings branch divisor. Our integral character criterion yields, in every dimension at least four, simply connected varieties of general type with 0-cycle Chow group \(\mathbb{Z}\), canonical volume four, and no birational product decomposition. We also determine optimal integral supports for componentwise product quotients and character decompositions of degree zero Chow groups. Within this covering class, we classify the minimum volume models and compute their pluricanonical map degrees.

papers.title: Gersten resolutions for logarithmic forms
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth variety over a field $k$ of characteristic 0. We show that (two versions of) the Zariski sheaves of regular $k$-linear logarithmic differential forms on $X$ (in the most na\"{\i}ve sense, i.e. sums of products of logarithmic differentials) have Gersten property (and therefore coincide). It turns out that the values of these sheaves are free abelian groups. As a consequence, for any integer $n>0$, these sheaves modulo $n$ also have Gersten property. The proof is an elementary application of the Voevodsky's $(-1)$-machinery and consists of assembling several well-known results.

papers.title: Superlinear regularity of Frobenius powers on a normal hypersurface
papers.abstract: We give answers to four questions on linear bounds for Frobenius powers. Let $\mathfrak m$ denote the homogeneous maximal ideal. We construct a height-two prime $I$ in a geometrically normal four-dimensional graded hypersurface $R$ of characteristic two such that, for every power $q\geq16$ of four, the Loewy length of $H^0_{\mathfrak m}(R/I^{[q]})$ is at least $q^{3/2}/8-1$. Thus no fixed integer $C$ gives annihilation by $\mathfrak m^{Cq}$ for all $q$, as required by the Hochster--Huneke condition $(\mathrm{LC})$. The same construction gives superlinear lower bounds for the Castelnuovo--Mumford regularity in Katzman's question, for the exponents of the embedded primary components in the question of Smith and Swanson, and for the degree in the least variable in Katzman's Gr\"obner basis conjecture. The bounds follow from the degree of the kernel line bundle of a multiplication pencil associated to a family of plane quartics.

papers.title: Generalizations of Igusa surfaces
papers.abstract: We give a criterion for the contracted product $E \times^G X$ to have a singular Picard scheme, where $E$ is an elliptic curve, $G \subset E$ is a finite subgroup scheme, and $X$ is a projective $G$-normal curve, in the sense of Brion. We show that every smooth projective surface with a singular Picard scheme and a positive-dimensional automorphism group scheme arises in this way. We also illustrate the criterion by constructing two new families of surfaces with singular Picard schemes, arising from $G$-normal curves $X$ for $G = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ and $G = \boldsymbol{\alpha}_p$, respectively. As a special case of $G = \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$, we recover Igusa's classical example. Finally, we compute all infinitesimal group schemes which appear as $\operatorname{Pic}^0_S/(\operatorname{Pic}^0_S)_{\mathrm{red}}$ for all (quasi)-bielliptic surfaces $S$. This completes the description of the singular Picard schemes of smooth projective surfaces of Kodaira dimension zero.

papers.title: The rank of the Fano normal function via the Fermat cubic
papers.abstract: We prove that the canonical derivative of the Fano normal function has rank ten at the Fermat cubic threefold. This yields a direct proof of its generic maximal rank, a result also implied by a general theorem of Gao--Zhang. Our approach combines Hain's equivariance principle with an explicit representation-theoretic computation and the nonvanishing of the Griffiths infinitesimal invariant established by Collino--Naranjo--Pirola.

papers.title: Sharp minima of higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated singularities
papers.abstract: We determine the minimum higher Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated complex polynomial singularities with fixed ambient dimension and multiplicity. A Fermat polynomial of multiplicity $m$, perturbed by the $(m+1)$-st power of a linear form, attains both minimum sequences at every order. These values remain the minima at each prescribed total degree $d>m$; the homogeneous case $d=m$ has a separate Tjurina formula. The proof expresses the Tjurina defect through multiplication in the filtered Milnor algebra and uses the monomial strong Lefschetz theorem to attain the resulting rank bound. We also determine the associated graded higher Tjurina algebras of this family and show that they are unchanged by terms of order at least $m+2$.

papers.title: Cylindricity of log del Pezzo surfaces in characteristic five
papers.abstract: Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic five, we prove that a log del Pezzo surface of Picard rank one contains no cylinder if it is not log liftable. We also characterize Du Val del Pezzo surfaces that contain no cylinder in positive characteristic.

papers.title: Lipschitz inner rates of normal surface singularities
papers.abstract: In this article, we connect the local Lipschitz geometry of a normal surface singularity with a rational homology sphere link to the analytic semigroup $S_{an}(\tilde{X})$ associated with a convenient resolution. Under certain restriction, we provide an explicit computational characterization of the Lipschitz rate $q_v$ associated with an irreducible exceptional curve $E_v$ in terms of the semigroup. We also show that removing the restriction we get examples when $q_v$ cannot be determined from the semigroup. Interestingly enough, this phenomenon already happens for rational singularities. Indeed, we exemplify that the inner rates of rational singularities are not topological.

papers.title: Derivations tangent to polar discriminants
papers.abstract: We describe the module of logarithmic derivations along the discriminant of a stable polar representation of a reductive algebraic group. It splits into derivations along the fibres of the quotient map and a free summand lifted from logarithmic derivations along the associated branch divisor. This gives a uniform extension of previous results on full adjoint discriminants. We prove that, for visible stable polar actions of semisimple groups with finite generic stabilizer, the discriminant is a free divisor. For stable periodic gradings of arbitrary order with semisimple degree-zero group, we construct explicit Saito matrices from the infinitesimal action and the gradients of basic invariants, which yields determinantal equations for several exceptional discriminants. In particular, starting with exceptional Lie algebras, we provide examples of free discriminants of degrees 60, 120, 126 and 240 for inner gradings and a degree-72 example for an outer one.

papers.title: $\lambda_g$-Integrals on triple, one-part admissible covers
papers.abstract: We effectively compute all intersection numbers of the form $\lambda_g\psi^d$ on moduli spaces of genus $g$ admissible covers with one point of full ramification and two additional branch points with arbitrary profile. We encode these invariants in appropriate generating functions, which we relate to the Hamiltonians of the KdV hierarchy.

papers.title: Semisimple Deformations of Contraction Algebras for Smooth Threefold Flops
papers.abstract: Building on Bryan--Katz--Leung, Hua--Toda and Kawamata, we study deformations of contraction algebras and the local geometry of the scheme of associative algebra laws. Let $A$ be the basic contraction algebra of a completed projective flopping contraction of a smooth complex threefold. We construct a finite free polynomial family that is constant and semisimple away from the origin, with the original curve projectors fixed. For each restricted positive root $\beta=(\beta_i)$, with coordinates indexed by the retained vertices, the split generic fibre has $n_\beta$ matrix blocks of size $\sum_i\beta_i$, and the labelled projector $e_i$ has rank $\beta_i$ on each block. Here $n_\beta$ is the corresponding genus-zero Gopakumar--Vafa invariant. If the geometric generic fibre of a finite free associative formal deformation of $A$ is semisimple, it has the same matrix factors, and any lifts of the original projectors have the same ranks on those factors. The scheme of associative algebra laws is smooth at $A$. The closure of the corresponding semisimple orbit is its unique irreducible component through $A$. The proof uses the curve divisors of Katz--Morrison and Nabijou--Wemyss, presentations of the universal contraction quotient and its cocenter, and the orbit method of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz. These presentations prove the geometric Hua--Toda flatness assertions. In the geometric families considered here, the relative contraction algebra, its centre and its cocenter are finite free over arbitrary complete Noetherian local complex bases. On a smooth open neighbourhood of $A$ in the scheme of algebra laws, the centres and cocenters form dual vector bundles compatible with arbitrary base change. For the type $D$ algebras $D_{n,2}$ with $n\ge2$, the centre morphism gives counterexamples to the smoothness assertion in Conjecture 1.4(2) of Jelisiejew--Smoktunowicz.

papers.title: Rigidity does not imply substitution rigidity
papers.abstract: We obtain a negative answer to a question of Freudenburg concerning rigidity conditions for a polynomial. We construct a polynomial that does not lie in the kernel of any nonzero locally nilpotent derivation on the polynomial ring, but there exist an affine domain, algebraically independent elements and a locally nilpotent derivation such that the result of substituting elements into the polynomial lies in the kernel of that locally nilpotent derivation, but at least one of the substituted elements does not lie in that kernel.

papers.title: On the Cohomological Amplitude of the Locally Analytic Jacquet--Langlands Functor
papers.abstract: We prove a local cohomological bound $R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(X,\mathcal F)\in D^{[0,\dim X]}$ for a pro-\'etale sheaf with a derived $p$-complete integral lattice whose modulo $p^m$ reductions are filtered colimits of finite local systems on an affinoid topologically of finite type over $C$. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, with $n\geq2$ and $F/\mathbb Q_p$ finite, we apply these local bounds to variants of Scholze's Jacquet--Langlands functor $\mathrm{JL}_\mathscr{B}(\Pi):= R\Gamma_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}(\mathbb{P}^{n-1}_C,\mathcal{F}_{\Pi}\otimes^{L, \square}_{\mathbb{Q}_p}\mathscr{B})$ for $\mathscr{B}\in\{\mathbb{Q}_p, \widehat{\mathscr{O}}, \mathbb{B}_J\}$ and Banach or compact-type LB representations $\Pi$ of $G$, obtaining $\mathrm{JL}_{\mathscr{B}}(\Pi)\in D^{[0,2(n-1)]}$ for each choice of $\mathscr{B}$. We also prove that for arbitrary continuous principal series $I(\eta)=(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)^{\mathrm{cont}}$, we have $\mathrm{JL}(\mathrm{Ind}_B^G\eta)\in D^{[0, n]}$, while $\mathrm{JL}_{\widehat{\mathscr{O}}}(I(\eta)),\mathrm{JL}_{\mathbb{B}_J}(I(\eta))\in D^{[0, n-1]}$.
